chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated, from Yaʿqūb, from Abī Hammām, from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام, concerning...

Regarding the menstruating woman: if she performs ghusl during the time of ʿaṣr, she prays ʿaṣr and then prays ẓuhr. This also does not conflict with what we presented earlier, because he only informed about one who performs ghusl during the time of ʿaṣr, and it is possible that she had become pure during the time of ẓuhr but delayed the ghusl until she performed ghusl at a time in which ʿaṣr had become constrained. For that reason, he instructed her to perform ẓuhr after she prays ʿaṣr.

key_terms.الْغُسْلَ: the ritual bath required after menstruation
key_terms.وَقْتِ الْعَصْرِ: the time of the ʿaṣr prayer

ai.seo_question: If a menstruating woman becomes pure and performs ghusl in the time of ʿaṣr, which prayer should she perform first?
ai.summary: This passage explains a legal ruling concerning a menstruating woman who becomes pure and performs ghusl during the time of ʿaṣr. It clarifies that praying ʿaṣr before ẓuhr in this case does not contradict earlier reports, because the delay may have occurred after purity was attained while the remaining time for ʿaṣr had become limited.
